correctness.rationale: Independently checked the linear iff and the cyclic-to-distinct reduction. For a start at a one and a positive final gap c, the two intermediate gap-end heights of the frequency chord are m−3a and 3c−m. Strict positivity puts all proper prefix densities above, and all proper suffix densities below, the overall density. Conversely, if a≥c, the length c+1 factors each contain one one. If a<c and 2a≥b+c, lengths a+1 and 2a+2 capture respectively one and two ones: the latter lies between b+c+2 and n−1. In the last case 2c≤a+b with a<c, lengths 2c+2 and c+1 capture respectively two and one ones. Thus equality with the chord is excluded too. Other starts must have differing end letters; reversal exchanges the two gap inequalities, giving exactly one start per strict crossing, which still works at a zero gap since a required positive end gap is the larger gap. A nontrivial repetition would repeat the block three times, forcing all gaps equal and no qualified rotation. Burnside gives (binom(m+2,2)+2δ_m)/3; in m=3q the q positive progression steps each give two cyclic orderings. The all-ones necklace is covered by the equal-gap case. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; proof gives the all-length result.
residual_risks: No claim for more than three markers, undirected bracelets, or equal-length Abelian borders.
